source_refs.note: Exercise 3.5, Question 14: one integral from three given conditions (printed (i)-(iii)); book p. 102. Key on p. 300 under 'Exercise 3.2'.

blocks.prompt: 14 Given the function \(f(x)\) satisfies the following conditions: (i) \(\int_{0}^{4} f(x)\,dx = 12\) (ii) \(f(4 - x) = f(x)\) (iii) \(f(x + 2) = f(x)\). Evaluate \(\int_{-1}^{5} f(x)\,dx\). [The printed (i)-(iii) are the three given conditions, so this question has one answer.]
blocks.explanation:
Condition (iii) says \(f\) repeats every 2 units (period 2).
Use it to get \(\int_0^2 f\) from \(\int_0^4 f = 12\), then cut \([-1, 5]\) into \([-1, 0]\), \([0, 4]\), \([4, 5]\) and shift the end pieces into \([0, 2]\).
Condition (ii) is not needed for the total.
steps:
Given: (i) \(\int_0^4 f(x)\,dx = 12\), (ii) \(f(4 - x) = f(x)\), (iii) \(f(x + 2) = f(x)\).
To find: \(\int_{-1}^{5} f(x)\,dx\).
Method: Property III to split, and substitutions \(x = t \pm 2\), \(x = t + 4\) together with the period 2.

Split \([-1, 5]\)
\[\int_{-1}^{5} f = \int_{-1}^{0} f + \int_{0}^{4} f + \int_{4}^{5} f\]
Why: Property III; the middle piece is known (12).

Shift the left piece (\(x = t - 2\))
\[\int_{-1}^{0} f(x)\,dx = \int_{1}^{2} f(t - 2)\,dt\]
\[= \int_{1}^{2} f(t)\,dt\]
Why: \(f(t) = f((t - 2) + 2) = f(t - 2)\) by (iii); limits \(-1, 0\) become 1, 2.

Shift the right piece (\(x = t + 4\))
\[\int_{4}^{5} f(x)\,dx = \int_{0}^{1} f(t + 4)\,dt\]
\[= \int_{0}^{1} f(t)\,dt\]
Why: using (iii) twice, \(f(t + 4) = f(t + 2) = f(t)\).

Check with an example
\[f(x) = 3 + 2\cos \pi x:\ \int_{0}^{4} f = 12,\quad \int_{-1}^{5} f = 18 \;\checkmark\]
Why: this \(f\) has period 2 and \(f(4 - x) = f(x)\); the cosine part integrates to 0 over whole periods, so the integrals are \(3 \times 4\) and \(3 \times 6\). Shortcut: \([-1, 5]\) is 3 periods, \(3 \times 6 = 18\). The key prints 18.
